thread.title: Qualcomm: Higher Broadcom Bid Looks More Likely, Says RBC

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Qualcomm: Higher Broadcom Bid Looks More Likely, Says RBC
text:
Shares of wireless technology giant Qualcomm ( QCOM ) are down 13 cents at $67.19, after RBC Capital Markets ’s Amit Daryanani this morning reiterated an Outperform rating on the shares, and raised his price target to $80 from $77, writing that he sees "increasing probability that AVGO will submit a higher offer” in its hosti;le bid for the company, which, you’ll recall, was a mix of cash and stock for $70 per Qualcomm share.
Daryanani’s note comes ahead of Qualcomm’s fiscal Q1 report this Thursday, after market close.
Writes Daryanani, "At face value, the AVGO bid at $70 ($60/ $10 cash/ stock) provides ~3% implied upside."
"We further think there is increasing probability that AVGO will submit a higher bid recently as March 6th is QCOM's shareholder meeting.”
The shareholder meeting , of course, is when Broadcom has asked Qualcomm shareholders to replace Qualcomm’s entire board with Broadcom’s candidates.
"We believe at this point AVGO is waiting for: 1) Better visibility on QCOM's progress with MOFCOM, 2) QCOM's action on its current $110 offer for NXPI,” referring to the bid by Qualcomm for NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), which has been working its way through approvals for over a year now.
Qualcomm may make an enhanced pitch for itself as an independent entity when it addresses the Street on Thursday, he expects:
We think high probability that QCOM will spend time convincing shareholders during their EPS call and beyond on their ability to achieve $6.00+ EPS (noted potential for $6.75-7.50 post AAPL resolution) and execute on cost take out initiatives. We think beyond QCOM EPS call on 1/31 the key will be to watch progress towards closing NXPI (recently received approvals from EU and South Korea, which leaves MOFCOM the last regulatory hurdle).
Another perspective today is offered by Bernstein ’s Stacy Rasgon , who has a Market Perform rating on the shares. He thinks that results for the December quarter should roughly meet the consensus for $5.92 billion in revenue and 91 cents per share.
However, he thinks the Street is not properly factoring in the continued withholding of royalties by Apple ’s ( AAPL ) manufacturers while their legal dispute is ongoing:
While modeling QTL is now more challenging given lower transparency we believe the Street may not be appropriately accounting for the fact that QCOM is no longer getting paid licensing by AAPL (traditionally the biggest source of strong March-Q QTL seasonality) as well as Dec-Q China 3G/4G handset shipments that appear exceptionally weak vs history. We model similar results for FY2018 ($23.1B/$3.27 vs consensus $22.9B/$3.48), and note QCOM's own recently-offered FY2019 guidance suggests deterioration to fundamentals vs expectations (we believe potentially from core business headwinds as well as the possibility of higher tax rates). Note that our numbers do not include NXPI, or any impact from the forthcoming $1B cut.
